q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'approximate earnings' from 'accounted earnings' of the Railways?

options.A: Approximate earnings relate to goods traffic only, whereas accounted earnings relate to coaching traffic only
options.B: Approximate earnings are compiled by the Railway Board, whereas accounted earnings are compiled by the stations
options.C: Approximate earnings are the final audited figures, whereas accounted earnings are provisional figures
options.D: Approximate earnings are the provisional figures compiled at short intervals from the station returns, before internal check and apportionment, whereas accounted earnings are the final figures brought to account after check and apportionment, as compiled in the Traffic Book

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, Major Heads 8658 (Suspense Accounts) and 8675 (Deposits with Reserve Bank) fall under the 'Suspense and Miscellaneous' section of the Public Account of India.
2. Major Head 8782 (Cash Remittances and adjustments between officers rendering accounts to the same accounting authority) falls under the 'Remittances' section of the Public Account of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Supplementary estimates for expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India are presented to the Lok Sabha along with the Supplementary Demands for Grants.
2. Like all charged expenditure, such charged supplementary estimates are not submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Commission is constituted by the President at the expiration of every fifth year, or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary.
2. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are binding on the Government of India and must be implemented without any modification.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Estimates Committee takes up for examination the estimates of only such Ministries, departments or subjects as it selects each year, and not the estimates of all the Ministries in a single year.
2. The Estimates Committee itself votes the Demands for Grants after examining them, whereafter the Lok Sabha passes them without further discussion.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Balance Sheet of the Railways, the balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads are netted head-wise and only the net balance under each head is shown.
2. Credit balances under such heads, representing amounts payable by the Railways, are shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

q: The subsidiary books of a railway, in which the transactions are first recorded in detail before being compiled into the General Books, are also known as the books of:

options.A: Final entry
